title: Kleinmond inniebos Kunstefees (KliK)
summary: Three days, multiple venues, one small seaside town. KliK 2026 takes over Kleinmond from 27 to 29 November.
description:
Three days, multiple venues, one small seaside town. KliK 2026 takes over Kleinmond from 27 to 29 November. Expect poetry, music, theatre, storytelling and art — built for anyone who loves words, music and the people who make them.
KliK 2026 brings together acclaimed writers, poets, storytellers, musicians, publishers, and artists for a vibrant celebration of language, culture and creativity. Across multiple venues, enjoy author talks, storytelling sessions, a writing workshop, poetry and music performances, a Writers' Café, Sip & Paint, and a guided Strandlooper Kruie Kuier experience.
Alongside the ticketed programme, a full weekend of free activity runs for the community. There's the KliK Market, a children and youth programme at Mthimkhulu, the See en Fynbos Paradys walk along Kleinmond's coastline, and an Open Mic.
Choose a 3-day or 2-day pass for the full run, a single day pass, or tickets to individual sessions. Multi-day passes work out far cheaper than buying sessions one at a time.
Whether you're an avid reader, aspiring writer, creative thinker or simply looking for an inspiring weekend by the sea, KliK 2026 has something for you.
27–29 November 2026 | Kleinmond, Western Cape
profile: KliK is a three-day arts festival across venues in Kleinmond, with poetry, music, theatre, storytelling, author talks, a writing workshop, a Writers' Café, Sip & Paint and a guided Strandlooper herb walk. Alongside the ticketed programme there is a free KliK Market, a children and youth programme, a coastal walk and an open mic. It suits readers, writers and anyone wanting a creative weekend by the sea; passes are sold for three days, two days, one day or single sessions.

title: Rosoberry Harvest Fest
summary: Join Rosoberry Nursery & Hermanus River Farm for the second Rosoberry Harvest Fest on 28 November 2026 – a relaxed, fun-filled family day celebrating berries, good food, music and summer on the farm.
description:
Join Rosoberry Nursery & Hermanus River Farm for the second Rosoberry Harvest Fest on 28 November 2026 – a relaxed, fun-filled family day celebrating berries, good food, music and summer on the farm.
Harvest Fest falls at the peak of our berry season. In the week leading up to the festival, we leave much of the fruit on the bushes so you can taste blackberries, youngberries, blueberries and pepinos at different stages of ripeness – including intensely flavoursome over-ripe berries that are only truly enjoyed straight from the bush, never bought in a supermarket. There may be a few special berries which only the early open eyed will find such as alpine strawberries and pink lemonade actually pink blueberries!
Come hungry, bring a picnic blanket & camping chair, explore the farm and settle in for the day.
Enjoy pick-your-own berries, farm-to-table food, HRF grass-fed beef, local wines, Belgian-style ales, coffee, ice cream, live music, kids' activities, tractor rides, plants and fresh farm produce.
NO OUTSIDE FOOD OR DRINK MAY BE BROUGHT INTO THE VENUE. NO PETS ALLOWED.
## Tickets
Adults R200 | Kids R70
## Limited to 500 people – book early to avoid missing out.
## Your ticket includes
• Farm entrance & parking
• Access to the 2.5 km Waterfall Walking Trail
• BERRIES! On arrival every guest receives an empty punnet to fill with berries you pick yourself, and the first 300 guests will also receive a full punnet of freshly picked berries. Everyone is welcome to pick and eat as many berries as they like throughout the day. Additional full or empty punnets will be available for purchase.
• Face painting 11am - 2pm, with an additional face painter assisting this year to keep the queue moving
• Tractor rides & lawn games
• Live music throughout the day with Craig Vee, Takura Terry, Lovecats, Mike Fabricius and Marcus Rosochacki
• Plenty of picnic space on the green pastures overlooking our herd of beef cattle
Bring your picnic blanket and umbrella and find a spot beneath the trees, stretch tent or out on the soft grass. Some blankets will be available.
Come early if you want the very best choice of berries on the bushes!
## Eat & drink on the farm
This year's food offering is bigger, while remaining deliberately local and small-scale.
Hermanus River Farm Boeries return for 2026, made with HRF grass-fed beef.
Janine, of Agteros Heritage Table from Stanford, will be serving slow-cooked brisket bowls and HRF beef espetadas.
The Poke Oukie joins us with fresh poke bowls.
Mariejo is joining with delicious Korean fusion pancakes, kimchi and healthy snacks.
I Scream You Scream Ice Cream returns with something cold for a summer afternoon.
Honingklip Brewery will be pouring its Belgian-style ales, including a special Blackberry Wit for Harvest Fest.
Gabriëlskloof will be pouring local wine.
And this year Hermanus River Farm will run its own farm produce stall, with fresh seasonal produce from the farm available to take home.
Rosoberry will also have a selection of berry plants and other nursery plants available for sale.
## For the kids
Harvest Fest is very much a family day.
Alongside face painting (11am - 2pm), tractor rides, lawn games and plenty of space to run around, look out for Doodles – a little stall run by the next generation of the family, selling fun kids' crafts and other odds and ends.
## Walk to the waterfall
One of the highlights of Harvest Fest is the 2.5 km Waterfall Walking Trail through Hermanus River Farm which will be guided by Dr Rosochacki at 11h30.
The path winds through an old eucalyptus forest in a shady valley before emerging into recovering fynbos that has been painstakingly restored following years of severe alien infestation.
At the end you'll discover one of the farm's special places: a dramatic waterfall framed by a small pocket of ancient Afromontane forest.
Please note: this is a genuine farm and mountain walking trail rather than a manicured garden path. There are steep, uneven and potentially slippery sections. Suitable footwear and a reasonable level of mobility are recommended. Children should be supervised.
profile: The second Rosoberry Harvest Fest at Hermanus River Farm is a family day at the peak of berry season, with pick-your-own berries, farm-to-table food, local wine, Belgian-style ales and live music. Visitors pick berries, take a guided 2.5 km waterfall trail through restored fynbos, and children get face painting, tractor rides and lawn games. It suits families; tickets are limited to 500 people, and no outside food, drink or pets are allowed.

title: The Stanford Stumble
summary: A fun-filled family day out created to raise funds and awareness for the Butterfly Centre School NPO.
description:
STANFORD STUMBLE
Walk • Run • Stumble • Laugh • Celebrate
28 November 2026 | Stanford Hills | 12:00–18:00
COME AS YOU ARE. STUMBLE AS YOU LIKE.
The Stanford Stumble is back — but this year, we’re doing things a little differently.
This isn’t a race.
Everyone is a winner.
There are no finish times to beat.
And nobody is keeping score.
The Stanford Stumble is a fun-filled family day out created to raise funds and awareness for the Butterfly Centre School NPO, a very special school supporting children who think and learn differently and therefore, don’t fit comfortably into mainstream education.
The Butterfly Centre relies solely on fundraising and the generosity of its community to continue doing what it does — giving children a place where they are understood, supported, celebrated and allowed to learn in a way that works for them.
So come and support an incredible cause while having a ridiculously good time doing it.
THE STUMBLE
Gather your family and friends, put together your most outrageous outfit and take on our 3 km route through the beautiful Stanford Hills farm.
You can:WALK IT.RUN IT.STUMBLE IT.
Or take your sweet time and simply enjoy the day.
Along the route, you’ll discover a series of surprise stations. Think of them as your very own Stumble goodie bags — you won’t know exactly what’s waiting for you until you get there.
Expect colour, refreshments, treats, surprises and plenty of opportunities to stop, laugh and make memories along the way.
And remember…
It’s not about how quickly you get there. It’s about enjoying the journey.
BACK ON THE LAWN
Once you’ve made your way back to Stanford Hills, the fun continues.
Settle onto the lawn, grab something to eat and drink, let the kids loose and enjoy the afternoon together.
The Butterfly Centre children will be helping to run the kids’ entertainment area, giving everyone the opportunity to meet some of the wonderful young people at the heart of the cause we’re supporting.
We’ll also have:
* ??? A Raffle draw
* ?? Live music by Rivertones
* ?? Kids’ entertainment
* ?? Ridiculous outfits
* ?? Colour and surprises
* ?? Treats and refreshments
* ?? Beautiful Stanford Hills surroundings
* ?? A whole lot of community spirit
There will also be a special word from Jami, owner and founder of the Butterfly Centre, sharing more about the school, its children and why this fundraiser matters so much.
COME FOR THE FUN. STAY FOR THE CAUSE.
The Stanford Stumble isn’t about being the fastest, fittest or most competitive person in the room.
It’s about bringing people together.
It’s about families spending a day outdoors.
It’s about dressing up and being a little ridiculous.
It’s about laughing with your friends.
It’s about celebrating our differences.
And most importantly, it’s about helping create a future where every child has a place where they belong.
CELEBRATE EVERYONE. EXACTLY AS THEY ARE.
profile: The Stanford Stumble is a fundraising family day for the Butterfly Centre School at Stanford Hills: a 3 km fancy-dress walk, run or stumble with surprise stations and no finish times. Afterwards people relax on the lawn with food, drinks, a raffle, live music by Rivertones and kids' entertainment. It suits families and groups of friends who want a fun day for a good cause.

title: TITAN Trail Run | Benguela Cove Lagoon Wine Estate
summary: Titan Trail Running is about well-built routes, great locations, and a community of runners who enjoy being out there.
description:
## Welcome to Titan Trail Running
Let’s Hit the Trails
If you love running, a bit of adventure, and the kind of routes that make your legs work but leave you smiling at the finish, you’re in the right place.
Titan Trail Running is about well-built routes, great locations, and a community of runners who enjoy being out there. Whether you’re chasing a podium or just keen for a solid morning on the trails, there’s a place for you on our start line.
And yes, walking is allowed on all distances. Run it, hike it, race it. Just get it done.
## What You Can Expect
### Proper Trails
Each event features carefully mapped routes designed to be interesting, runnable, and rewarding. You can also expect water stations along the route to keep you hydrated.
### Accurate Timing
Your race, your result. We time every event so you can track your performance and see where you stack up [ and get your Vitality points ;) ]
### Podiums & Medals
If you’re fast, we’ll celebrate you properly. If you’re not, you still earn your medal, and your bragging rights.
### Post-Run Atmosphere
Titan events are designed to be more than a start and finish line. Expect:
- Great coffee
- Good food
- Wine at selected venues
- Space to sit, relax, and enjoy the vibe
We want you to stick around after you’ve crossed the line!
### Professional Support
Medical teams are on standby at every event, and our routes are clearly marked and well managed so you can focus on running.
### Cool Partners
We have some really cool partners we invite to display their awesome product on the day. They are there for you to make your running experience amazing.
For a cool discount on the best electrolytes on the market, use code: Titan20 here -> sci_coreSALT to be race ready on the day!
### Good Vibes Only
No egos. No pressure. Just people who enjoy being active, being outdoors, and being part of something well organised.
## Our Venues
Titan Trail Running takes place at standout locations across the Western Cape.
Each event location brings its own flavour, but the Titan standard stays the same: solid routes, great scenery, and a welcoming atmosphere.
## Distances & Format
We offer accessible distances:
- 5KM - Start at 07:45
- 10KM - Start at 07:30
Wave starts keep things flowing, with early morning kick-offs to make the most of the day.
### Registration
Registration open at 06:30, make sure to come early to collect you timing band at the registration booth (look out for the TITAN gazebo). You only need your full name to register.
So what do you say?
Sign up. Show up. Bring your people.
Let’s hit the trails together.
profile: A TITAN trail run at Benguela Cove Lagoon Wine Estate with 5 km and 10 km distances, starting from 07:30 after registration opens at 06:30. Runners and walkers follow marked, timed routes with water stations, then stay for coffee, food and wine. It suits trail runners of any pace.

title: The Stanford 100 Miler
summary: The Stanford 100 Miler is a 1 day dirt road bicycle race in the heart of the Overstrand.
description:
The Stanford 100 Miler is a 1 day dirt road bicycle race in the heart of the Overstrand.
All bicycles welcome. Gravel, MTB or E-bike
Did you know Stanford is the only Town in the Overstrand proclaimed a Heritage Site, in its entirety. Like the whole Town is a Heritage site.
Fancy.
Probably the best part of Stanford is its proximity to equally beautiful towns, Gansbaai, Pearly Beach, Hermanus, Franskraal, Elim, Baarskeedersbos and L’Agulhas, the Southernmost tip of Africa.
The Stanford 100 Miler, brought to you by the people who bring you one-of-a-kind bicycle race in the Tankwa Karoo, The Tanqua Kuru Bicycle Race
This race has been built from the ground up. Fresh. Real. Untemplacised with an unwavering commitment to create memories and adding value to the people who host us.
Join us for The Hunt.
Tally-ho!
NB Timing:
Timing will be managed by Finish Time. No Finish Time Timing Board - no ride.
Route:
Start & finish will be at the lush The Stanford Hills Estate
100 Miler - 169km - 2358m elevation - Start 07:30 - Strict enforced 10 hour cut-off
50 Miler - 77km - 1365m elevation - Start 08:30 - Strict enforced 6 hour cut-off
25 Miler - 40km - 500m elevation - Start 09:30 - Strict enforced 4 hour cut-off
This course favours the rouleur who is sharp enough to leave a bit in the tank for a few of the clever twists and turns towards the business end of the course.
After a short neutral section out of Town, hunters will immediately head South on some pristine gravel. Clay hardpack is the name of the game while you zig zag along the Uilkraals River.
You’ll eventually head in a Northerly direction and this is where the fun really begins. Rural, tarmac like gravel roads with two ‘bumps’ ready to the pack of the laggards. Over-cook the wet clay downhill sections here and it's not only new bike day, but also new clavicle day. More slippery than a greased weasel.
Get your steed over the last bump and all that's left is to channel your inner puncheur to the line.
The hounds will meet you at the village pub to revel in your success.
Tally-ho!

profile: The Stanford 100 Miler is a one-day dirt-road bicycle race from Stanford Hills Estate, open to gravel bikes, mountain bikes and e-bikes, over 169 km, 77 km or 40 km routes.
